title: Oracle Stock Crashes After OpenAI's Revenue Gap. Who's Next?
key_facts: Oracle shares fell more than 5% on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 after a Financial Times report raised questions about OpenAI's sales.
The FT report put OpenAI's annualised revenue near $50 billion at the end of September, against the $70 billion previously reported.
The article says the gap largely reflects differences in how revenue is calculated and does not mean OpenAI lost $20 billion in sales.
Oracle reportedly signed a $300 billion, five-year cloud computing deal with OpenAI in September 2025, roughly 45% of its $664 billion backlog of contracted future revenue.
Oracle's latest quarter showed $28.5 billion in capital spending and negative free cash flow of $5.4 billion.
The Wall Street Journal reported Oracle is exploring more financing for AI chips; Oracle says AI cloud demand 'continues to grow faster than supply'.
Broadcom fell nearly 4%, Nvidia more than 2% and Microsoft more than 1%.
quote_evidence: However, the $20 billion gap largely reflects differences in revenue calculations.
Oracle has become heavily dependent on OpenAI's future spending.
why_it_matters_hint: Oracle is singled out because a large part of its future revenue depends on one customer, OpenAI.
notes: The Yahoo Finance page carries a BeInCrypto article by Mohammad Shahid ("Read the Original story ... at beincrypto.com"); the BeInCrypto original link was not available, so the url is the Yahoo page. Overlaps C07-01 and C07-03 (same OpenAI revenue story) but adds the Oracle angle.
